metadata.case_name: CHAN CHEUK KI AND ANOTHER v. POON YU CHEUNG AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: fracture of the calcaneum of both heels
source: fracture of the calcaneum of both heels.
On his transfer the same day to PMH the above fractures were confirmed and an operation on both feet took place on 14th November, with bone grafting, open reduction and plating.
X rays revealed a healed but deformed calcaneum in both heels.
old fractures and disruptions to the subtalar joints of both heels, and signs of osteoarthritis in both heels.

injuries.description: fractured calcaneum of the left heel
source: x-rays revealed a fractured calcaneum of the left heel.
He suffered an operation on 15th November 1988 for reduction, fixing and bone grafting of the fracture.
X-rays showed healing of the original fracture, but with residual deformities and a slight misalignment of the subtalar joint.

injuries.description: lacerated wound about 1.5 cm deep on the forehead
source: a lacerated wound about 1.5 cm deep on the forehead
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

manifestations.description: Inability to walk for more than two hours due to heel pain
Restriction in both heels of all normal movements
Disruptions to the subtalar joints of both heels
Signs of osteoarthritis in both heels
Distortion to the shape of both heels
Restriction in the movements of the subtalar and ankle joints
Stiffness; restriction from running, jumping, walking on uneven ground and squatting
Was in a wheelchair for 4-5 months after the accident
Widening of the heel area and rigidity of the subtalar joint with minimal movement
Left foot marginally shorter than the right, probably due to a shortening of the fracture
Tendinitis due to pressure from the widened heel
Pain on weight bearing in walking

treatments_future: renew foot orthotics every three years
possible cortisone injections for tendon inflammation (as needed)

losses.description: pain on weight bearing and stiffness causing difficulty in climbing/descending stairs and inability to perform excessive walking

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: restricted from running, jumping, walking on uneven ground and squatting
assigned mostly indoor and light work and unable to climb ladders, carry heavy weights, work on scaffolding or work outdoors
considered unfit to return to the same work due to the heel condition
